title: Clinical Benefits of Exogenous Ketosis in Adults with Disease: A Systematic Review
summary: Systematic review of exogenous ketosis studies in adults with medical conditions. The paper evaluates clinical efficacy, disease-domain outcomes, adverse events, evidence limitations, and the need for larger trials rather than synthesizing ketone-body mechanism as the main contribution.
full_text: The review follows PRISMA-style clinical evidence synthesis across neurological, metabolic, cardiovascular, psychiatric, and inflammatory conditions. Biological and metabolic rationale is background. The center of gravity is patient-facing clinical benefit and evidence quality in adults with disease.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled clinical because the main question is clinical benefit and evidence quality in adult disease populations; mechanistic rationale is not the primary contribution.

title: Alzheimer blood biomarkers: practical guidelines for study design, sample collection, processing, biobanking, measurement and result reporting
summary: Guideline-style paper for Alzheimer blood biomarker studies. It focuses on study design, blood collection, processing, biobanking, biomarker measurement, result reporting, and standardization of preanalytical, analytical, and post-analytical practice.
full_text: The paper provides practical guidance and an SOP-oriented framework for high-quality blood-based Alzheimer biomarker research. It discusses clinical contexts, but the operational contribution is measurement workflow standardization rather than patient outcome estimation or causal disease biology.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the center of gravity is standardizing biomarker study workflow, collection, processing, biobanking, measurement, and reporting.

title: Preanalytical sample handling recommendations for Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers
summary: Experimental methods paper assessing how common preanalytical factors affect plasma Alzheimer biomarker measurements. It studies collection tubes, anticoagulants, time to centrifugation, storage, freeze-thaw cycles, tube transfers, and measurement stability.
full_text: The paper quantifies sample-handling effects on plasma amyloid and tau measurements using automated assays, then translates those findings into handling recommendations. The main contribution is preanalytical reliability and standardization for biomarker measurement.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper evaluates sample-handling variables and measurement reliability rather than clinical prognosis or Alzheimer mechanism.

title: Critical Factors in Sample Collection and Preparation for Clinical Metabolomics of Underexplored Biological Specimens
summary: Review article on preanalytical factors for sample collection and extraction of underexplored biological specimens in clinical metabolomics. It emphasizes protocol standardization, contamination avoidance, extraction choices, and practical design considerations for metabolomic experiments.
full_text: The review surveys collection and preparation issues for specimens such as breast milk, ocular fluids, sebum, seminal plasma, sweat, hair, saliva, and cerebrospinal fluid. Diagnostic and biomarker discovery applications are context; the center of gravity is metabolomics sample preparation and preanalytical method design.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the review synthesizes sample collection, extraction, and preparation practices for metabolomics rather than clinical outcome evidence or disease mechanism.

title: A single-cell and spatial RNA-seq database for Alzheimer's disease (ssREAD)
summary: Resource paper introducing ssREAD, a database for Alzheimer-related single-cell, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomics datasets. It emphasizes dataset curation, metadata annotation, usability, and an analysis suite for clustering, differential expression, marker genes, regulons, and spatial deconvolution.
full_text: The paper includes AD biological examples, but its primary contribution is a reusable database and analysis resource that aggregates many datasets and exposes workflows for exploring them. Disease biology is demonstrated through the resource rather than being the sole central claim.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper's primary contribution is a reusable database and analysis resource, not a new causal pathway or patient-facing clinical claim.

title: Single-cell multiregion dissection of Alzheimer's disease
summary: Single-nucleus multi-region atlas study of post-mortem human brain samples across Alzheimer disease progression. It profiles more than one million nuclei across brain regions and uses the atlas to identify cell types, gene programs, vulnerability, response, and resilience patterns in Alzheimer pathology.
full_text: The paper provides an online resource, but the central scientific contribution is biological interpretation of AD progression across brain regions, neuronal and glial subtype changes, pathology-associated gene programs, and mechanisms of vulnerability and resilience.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled mechanism because the resource is primarily used to make mechanistic disease-biology claims about cell states, vulnerability, response, and resilience in Alzheimer disease.

title: The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews
summary: Reporting guideline paper updating PRISMA for systematic reviews. It defines required reporting items and updated guidance for transparent review methods, synthesis, data availability, and reporting completeness rather than evaluating a specific clinical intervention.
full_text: The paper is about how systematic reviews should be reported and what methodological information should be included. Clinical examples and evidence-synthesis contexts are background; the contribution is a reporting checklist and methodological standard.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the main contribution is a reporting guideline/checklist for systematic review methods, not clinical evidence about a disease.

title: STARD 2015: an updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies
summary: Reporting guideline paper updating the STARD checklist for diagnostic accuracy studies. It lists essential items to improve transparency, appraisal, replication, and reporting completeness for studies of diagnostic tests.
full_text: Although diagnostic accuracy studies are patient-facing, this paper is not evaluating one diagnostic test. Its center of gravity is a reporting standard and checklist for diagnostic accuracy research.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper defines a reporting checklist for diagnostic accuracy studies rather than reporting diagnostic performance of a specific clinical test.

title: Transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis (TRIPOD): the TRIPOD Statement
summary: Reporting guideline paper for multivariable prediction models in prognosis or diagnosis. It provides minimum reporting recommendations for studies developing or validating prediction models rather than presenting a specific patient cohort result.
full_text: The title contains prognosis and diagnosis, but the object of synthesis is model-reporting methodology. The contribution is a checklist for reproducible reporting of prediction model development and validation.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper is a reporting standard for prediction model studies, not a clinical prognostic model result.

title: MIFlowCyt: The minimum information about a flow cytometry experiment
summary: Minimum-information standard for reporting flow cytometry experiments. It specifies the sample, instrumentation, data analysis, and experimental overview information needed for transparent sharing and interpretation of flow cytometry data.
full_text: The paper is a reporting and metadata standard for a biomedical assay technology. Biological or diagnostic use cases are context; the central contribution is standardizing how flow cytometry experiments are described.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper defines a reporting/metadata standard for flow cytometry experiments.

title: A survey of best practices for RNA-seq data analysis
summary: Methods review covering major steps in RNA-seq analysis, including experimental design, quality control, read alignment, quantification, visualization, differential expression, alternative splicing, functional analysis, fusion detection, and eQTL mapping.
full_text: The paper surveys analysis workflows and best practices for RNA-seq data. Any biological applications are examples; the contribution is a methods review of computational analysis choices.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the review synthesizes RNA-seq analysis workflow and best practices rather than a disease mechanism or patient outcome.

title: Guidelines for the use and interpretation of assays for monitoring autophagy (4th edition)
summary: Large methods guideline for selecting, interpreting, and critiquing assays that monitor autophagy and related processes. It addresses assay choice, pitfalls, interpretation limits, and experimental standards across organisms and systems.
full_text: Autophagy is a mechanistic biology topic, but this paper's object is assay use and interpretation. The center of gravity is methodological guidance for monitoring a biological process, not a new causal autophagy mechanism.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper provides assay-selection and interpretation guidelines for monitoring autophagy.

title: ClinVar: public archive of interpretations of clinically relevant variants
summary: Database/resource paper describing ClinVar as a public archive for submitted interpretations of variant clinical significance, supporting evidence, accessioning, aggregation, standards, and programmatic access.
full_text: The paper concerns the structure, submission model, standards, access, and maintenance of a variant-interpretation archive. It is a biomedical informatics resource rather than a clinical cohort study or mechanistic variant analysis.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the contribution is a public data archive and informatics resource for variant interpretations.

title: Open Targets Platform: supporting systematic drug-target identification and prioritisation
summary: Database/platform paper describing Open Targets as a resource integrating target, disease, phenotype, drug, genetic, pathway, expression, text-mining, and animal-model evidence to support drug target identification and prioritization.
full_text: The paper is about the platform data model, evidence integration, scoring, curation, and programmatic/user access. Drug discovery and disease biology are use cases; the contribution is an informatics resource.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the main contribution is an integrated platform/resource for target-disease evidence and prioritization.

title: The Molecular Signatures Database Hallmark Gene Set Collection
summary: Resource paper introducing the Hallmark gene set collection in MSigDB. It reduces redundancy among gene sets through computational and expert curation to support more robust gene set enrichment analysis.
full_text: The paper is centered on constructing and curating a reusable gene-set resource for downstream enrichment analysis. Biological processes and diseases are represented in the database, but the contribution is a methods/resource layer.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper creates a curated analysis resource for gene set enrichment rather than testing a disease mechanism.

title: The Gene Ontology knowledgebase in 2023
summary: Resource paper describing the Gene Ontology knowledgebase, including structured vocabularies, gene product annotations, updates, tools, and guidance for computational use of gene function data.
full_text: The paper's main contribution is maintenance and description of a standardized knowledgebase used for functional interpretation and computational analysis. It is not a primary mechanistic study of one pathway or disease.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the contribution is a standardized gene-function knowledgebase and analysis resource.
